questions.stem: A client with profuse diarrhea tests positive for Clostridioides difficile. Which infection-control action should the nurse implement?

options.text: Use soap and water for hand hygiene after removing gloves.
Use alcohol-based sanitizer alone because it is faster.
Place the client on droplet precautions only.
Share the blood pressure cuff after wiping it with a dry towel.

questions.rationale: C. difficile spores are not reliably removed by alcohol-based hand rub alone, so soap-and-water hand hygiene is required after glove removal. Contact precautions and dedicated equipment are also important. Using only sanitizer or shared equipment increases transmission risk.

questions.stem: A client in labor has a sudden fetal heart rate drop after rupture of membranes and the nurse sees a loop of umbilical cord. Which immediate actions should the nurse take?
questions.scenario: The fetal heart rate remains in the 70s while help is being called.

options.text: Use a gloved hand to lift the presenting part off the cord
Position the client to relieve pressure on the cord
Attempt to push the visible cord back into the vagina
Delay intervention until the provider is at the bedside
Call for immediate obstetric assistance

questions.stem: A client is admitted with suspected bacterial meningitis. Which infection-control measure should the nurse implement first?

options.text: Initiate droplet precautions.
Place the client in airborne isolation.
Use reverse isolation to protect the client.
Delay precautions until a lumbar puncture confirms the diagnosis.

questions.rationale: Suspected bacterial meningitis requires prompt droplet precautions to reduce transmission risk. The nurse should not wait for confirmation before initiating appropriate isolation. Airborne or reverse isolation do not match the primary transmission risk for typical bacterial meningitis.

distractorRationales.b: "Place the client in airborne isolation" answers a lower-acuity part of the scenario. The cue "Suspected bacterial meningitis requires prompt droplet precautions to reduce transmission risk" raises concern for infection progression, so infection or sepsis escalation is needed before routine care.
distractorRationales.c: "Use reverse isolation to protect the client" misses the bedside risk. The cue "Start droplet precautions right away when bacterial meningitis is suspected" points to infection progression. Infection control or sepsis escalation limits spread and organ hypoperfusion before lower-acuity care.
distractorRationales.d: The safer response addresses infection progression; "Delay precautions until a lumbar puncture confirms the diagnosis" moves care toward routine observation before infection or sepsis escalation.

questions.takeaway: Start droplet precautions right away when bacterial meningitis is suspected.

questions.stem: Which decision map best explains the nurse's priority before this client receives IV contrast?
questions.scenario: A client with chronic kidney disease is scheduled for a contrast-enhanced CT study.
questions.additionalInfo: The nurse notes elevated creatinine and asks which prevention frame should guide care before transport.

options.text: Identify renal vulnerability, protect hydration and kidney-safe preparation, and watch post-contrast renal trends
Treat the study as risk-free because contrast only affects clients on dialysis
Delay hydration because IV fluids can interfere with the scanner
Ignore baseline creatinine as long as the client is not reporting pain

questions.rationale: Contrast prevention starts with recognizing renal vulnerability and supporting kidney-protective preparation, especially hydration and medication review when ordered. The nurse should not treat contrast risk as absent just because the client is stable at the bedside.

distractorRationales.b: "Treat the study as risk-free because contrast only affects clients on dialysis" misses the bedside risk. The cue "Contrast prevention starts with recognizing renal vulnerability and supporting kidney-protective preparation, especially hydration and medication review when ordered" points to medication toxicity. Medication safety depends on checking contraindications, labs, and adverse effects before giving or continuing the drug.
distractorRationales.c: "Delay hydration because IV fluids can interfere with the scanner" misses the bedside risk. The cue "The nurse notes elevated creatinine and asks which prevention frame should guide care before transport" points to medication toxicity. Medication safety depends on checking contraindications, labs, and adverse effects before giving or continuing the drug.
distractorRationales.d: This distractor shifts care toward premature activity instead of medication-safety intervention. The stem cue "The nurse notes elevated creatinine and asks which prevention frame should guide care before transport" makes medication toxicity the active safety concern.

questions.takeaway: Stable appearance does not erase contrast risk when the kidneys are already vulnerable.
questions.speedCue: High creatinine before contrast means prevention mode, not routine transport mode.

questions.stem: A client who recently started haloperidol develops severe muscle rigidity, a temperature of 104 F (40 C), and fluctuating blood pressure. Which action should the nurse take first?

options.text: Hold the antipsychotic and notify the provider about possible neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
Give the next dose early to stabilize behavior.
Apply extra blankets to reduce shivering.
Wait to see if the symptoms improve after sleep.

questions.rationale: Hyperthermia, rigidity, and autonomic instability after antipsychotic therapy are classic clues for neuroleptic malignant syndrome. The triggering drug should be stopped and emergency evaluation begun immediately. Delayed recognition can lead to rhabdomyolysis, renal injury, and death.

distractorRationales.b: The safer response addresses medication toxicity; "Give the next dose early to stabilize behavior" moves care toward routine care before medication-safety intervention.
distractorRationales.c: The safer response addresses medication toxicity; "Apply extra blankets to reduce shivering" moves care toward routine care before medication-safety intervention.
distractorRationales.d: The cue "Hyperthermia, rigidity" suggests medication toxicity, so "Wait to see if the symptoms improve after sleep" would not correct the active problem. Medication safety depends on checking contraindications, labs, and adverse effects before giving or continuing the drug.

questions.takeaway: Rigidity plus high fever after an antipsychotic is a stop-the-drug emergency pattern.
